seo.title: Resume Checklist for Senior Roles | VP Director Engineer Resume Guide | Rupesh Tiwari
seo.description: Complete resume checklist for VP, Director, Senior Manager, Staff Engineer, and Data Engineer roles. Learn what FAANG recruiters look for and how to format your resume for senior positions.

hero.title: The Resume Checklist for Senior Roles
hero.subtitle: What FAANG recruiters actually look for
hero.description: Your resume has 6 seconds to make an impression. At senior levels, the bar is even higher. I've reviewed 500+ resumes and helped professionals land at Amazon, Google, Meta, and more. Here's the checklist that works.

roles.title: VP / Vice President
roles.summary: VPs must show organizational impact, P&L responsibility, and strategic vision across multiple teams or business units.
mustHaves: Revenue or P&L impact ($X million influenced)
formatTips: 2 pages maximum, executive summary at top
Lead with business outcomes, not activities

roles.title: Director / Senior Director
roles.summary: Directors bridge strategy and execution. Show you can build teams, drive multi-team initiatives, and deliver measurable business results.
formatTips: Show progression (IC to Manager to Director)
Include team size and scope for each role
commonMistakes: Reading like an IC resume with 'manager' title

roles.title: Senior Manager / Engineering Manager
roles.summary: Senior Managers must show they can lead teams, deliver projects, and grow their people. Balance technical depth with leadership evidence.
mustHaves: Project delivery with timelines and outcomes
formatTips: Clearly state team sizes for each role
Include both technical and people achievements
Show progression from IC if applicable
commonMistakes: Only technical achievements, no people leadership
No metrics on delivery or team growth

roles.title: Staff / Principal Engineer
roles.summary: Staff+ engineers must show technical leadership beyond their team—architecture decisions, mentorship, and org-wide impact.
mustHaves: Technical standards or best practices established
Patents, papers, or tech talks (if applicable)
formatTips: Show technical leadership without direct reports
Include open source or community contributions
commonMistakes: Reading like a senior engineer resume

roles.title: Data Engineer / ML Engineer
roles.summary: Data engineers must show they can build scalable data systems, work with large datasets, and enable data-driven decisions.
formatTips: Quantify data volumes and processing times
commonMistakes: Missing business impact of data work

roles.title: Solutions Architect / CSM
roles.summary: Solutions Architects must show customer-facing skills, technical breadth, and ability to translate business needs to technical solutions.
commonMistakes: No revenue or deal size context

universalChecklist.title: Resume Checklist for All Senior Roles

checks: 1-2 pages maximum (1 page for <10 years experience)
Clean, ATS-friendly format (no tables, columns, or graphics)
Reverse chronological order within each section
Brief company description if not well-known
Delivery metrics (shipped X features, Y% on-time)
No acronyms without full form (first use)

faqs.question: How long should a VP or Director resume be?
faqs.answer: VP and Director resumes should be 1.5-2 pages maximum. Focus on the last 10-15 years of experience. Earlier roles can be summarized in 1-2 lines. Quality over quantity—every bullet should demonstrate leadership impact. If you're struggling to fit everything, it usually means you're including too much tactical detail.

faqs.question: Should I include a summary or objective statement?
faqs.answer: For senior roles, yes—include a 2-3 line executive summary at the top. This should highlight your leadership scope, industry expertise, and key achievements. Avoid generic statements like 'results-driven leader.' Instead: 'VP of Engineering with 15 years building and scaling teams from 10 to 200+ engineers across fintech and e-commerce, delivering $50M+ in annual revenue impact.'

faqs.question: How do I quantify impact if my company doesn't share metrics?
faqs.answer: Use estimates with qualifiers: 'approximately,' 'estimated,' or ranges. You can quantify team size, project scope, timelines, user growth, or relative improvements ('reduced latency by 40%'). If you truly can't quantify, describe scope: 'Led the company's largest cross-functional initiative' or 'Owned architecture serving 10M+ daily active users.'

faqs.question: Should I list all my technical skills as a Director or VP?
faqs.answer: No—for leadership roles, a brief technical skills section is fine, but it shouldn't dominate. Focus on technologies relevant to the role you're targeting. Better to demonstrate technical credibility through your experience bullets than list every language you've ever used. Example: 'Led migration from on-prem to AWS (EKS, Lambda, DynamoDB)' shows skills in context.

faqs.question: How do I show leadership on my resume if I don't have direct reports?
faqs.answer: Leadership isn't just about direct reports. Highlight: technical leadership (architecture decisions adopted by multiple teams), project leadership (led cross-functional initiatives), mentorship (grew junior engineers to senior), and influence (drove adoption of best practices across the org). Use language like 'led,' 'drove,' 'established,' 'influenced,' 'mentored.'

faqs.question: What's the right format for a Data Engineer resume?
faqs.answer: Data Engineer resumes should lead with a technical summary listing your primary stack (Spark, Kafka, Airflow, etc.) and cloud platforms. Each experience bullet should include scale metrics: data volume (TB/PB), processing frequency (real-time/batch), and business impact. Example: 'Built real-time pipeline processing 5TB/day, reducing analytics latency from hours to minutes and enabling $10M pricing optimization.'

faqs.question: How important are certifications for senior roles?
faqs.answer: Certifications matter more for some roles than others. For Solutions Architects and Cloud Engineers, AWS/GCP/Azure certifications are expected. For VPs and Directors, they're nice-to-have but not essential. For Staff+ Engineers, certifications are less important than demonstrated impact. Always list relevant certifications with dates to show currency.

faqs.question: Should I tailor my resume for each application?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially for senior roles where competition is fierce. Create a 'master resume' with all your experience, then tailor for each application: 1) Match keywords from the job description, 2) Reorder bullets to highlight relevant experience, 3) Adjust your summary to align with the role. Don't rewrite from scratch—strategic adjustments are enough.

faqs.question: How do I explain gaps or short tenures on my resume?
faqs.answer: Address gaps honestly in your cover letter or be prepared to discuss in interviews. For short tenures: if you have a pattern, it's a red flag; if it's one role, explain the context (acquisition, layoff, role mismatch). Don't hide gaps with creative date formatting—recruiters will notice. Focus on what you learned or accomplished during that time.

faqs.question: What's the difference between an Amazon resume and a Google resume?
faqs.answer: Amazon values 'Leadership Principles' language—weave LP keywords naturally (customer obsession, ownership, bias for action). Google values technical depth and innovation—highlight novel solutions and intellectual contributions. Both want quantified impact. Amazon often prefers more structured formats; Google is slightly more flexible. Tailor your emphasis, not your entire resume.
